subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY suppression for generic mixed trailing or contained payloads, and where should the boundary sit between silent-intent text and legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main deliberately preserves some substantive trailing-token replies while the issue asks for broader suppression to avoid internal text leaks; that is a shared message-delivery and security contract decision rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then reuse it across delivery paths.

options.title: Use blanket trailing/own-line suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line NO_REPLY token and accept that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the current narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, reasoning-prefixed, and selected scoped cases are suppressed, then close or retarget broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then reuse it across delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans shared reply delivery and security/product policy, and steipete is tied to recent classifier and central-file landing history.
